title: Fix the two offsets
starter:
%x  = buffer 16 dtype=i32 slot=0
%w  = buffer 4 dtype=i32 slot=1
%y  = buffer 9 dtype=i32 slot=2
%oi = range 3
%oj = range 3
%o3 = mul %oi 3
%yo = add %o3 %oj
%yv = shrink %y %yo []
%z  = store %yv 0
%y0 = after %y %z
%ki = range 2
%kj = range 2
%r  = add %oi %ki
%c  = add %oj %kj
%r4 = mul %r 3
%xo = add %r4 %c
%xv = shrink %x %xo []
%xe = load %xv
%k2 = mul %ki 1
%wo = add %k2 %kj
%wv = shrink %w %wo []
%we = load %wv
%p  = mul %xe %we
%yv0 = shrink %y0 %yo []
%cur = load %yv0
%sum = add %cur %p
%s  = store %yv0 %sum
%e1 = end %s %kj
%e2 = end %e1 %ki
%e3 = end %e2 %oj
%e4 = end %e3 %oi
%y1 = after %y %e4
hints: Two lines multiply by the wrong number. Each one turns a (row, column) pair into a flat offset, so ask of each: how many elements long is a row of this buffer?
The input `x` is 4 columns wide, so its element (r, c) is at `r*4 + c`. The kernel `w` is 2 columns wide, so its element (ki, kj) is at `ki*2 + kj`.
Change `%r4 = mul %r 3` to `mul %r 4` and `%k2 = mul %ki 1` to `mul %ki 2`. The output offset `oi*3 + oj` is already right, because `y` is 3 columns wide.
explain: Every buffer has its own row length: 4 for the input, 2 for the kernel and 3 for the output. The starter used 3 for the input and 1 for the kernel. Both wrong offsets still fit inside their buffers, so the bounds check passes and only the answers are wrong. That is why you check the row length of each buffer by hand.
